B1.1 Problem Specification

Define the problem before writing the solution

"Build a canteen app so lunch queues disappear."

A member of staff sends you this message. You have budget, a team, and a deadline.

What's missing before you write a single line of code?

Pulling a specification apart

Component Canteen app example
Problem statement Queue time averages 14 min; wrong orders are common.
Objectives Queue under 5 min, order errors near zero.
Constraints Limited budget, offline mode needed, allergy compliance.
Input / Output In: meal choice + student ID. Out: kitchen ticket + confirmation screen.
Evaluation criteria Measured by queue timing and mismatch logs.

Where does each one belong?

Sort these into the correct part of a problem specification:

  • "Must run on existing tablets."
  • "Staff need fewer manual steps."
  • "Average order confirmation under 10 seconds."
  • "Output includes allergy warning."

Then: draft a full spec from a school scenario — B1.1 worksheet, Activities section.

Whose version of "success" wins?

Students want speed. Kitchen staff want accuracy. Leadership wants cost control.

Same system, three different definitions of success. Now what?

Mapping who cares about what

Stakeholder Priority Risk if ignored
Students Fast ordering, reliable output Abandonment, queue crowding
Canteen staff Accurate tickets, clear flow Order rework, delays
School leaders Cost control, legal compliance Budget overrun, legal exposure

Budget just killed the barcode scanner

You can't afford the hardware. Something else has to give. Which one and why?

  • Interface speed target
  • Report detail in output
  • Number of optional features

Defend the choice using stakeholder impact, not personal preference.

Then: stakeholder conflict worksheet — Activities section.

"Make the app better."

How would you test whether that happened?

You can't. That's the problem.

Vague vs. testable

Vague Testable
The UI is good. 80% of students complete an order in under 45 seconds.
System is reliable. Failed transactions stay below 1% over one week.
Output is clear. Every kitchen ticket shows meal, allergens, and timestamp.

Your turn: make this testable

"The platform should work globally."

Rewrite it with at least one language constraint, one legal constraint, one input standard, and one measurable evaluation metric.

What fails first if you skip problem specification entirely?

Stakeholder alignment? Constraints handling? Success measurement?

Pick one. Defend it.
